name: correctness

findings.message: The JSON holder extraction in `zbuild_claim_acquire` uses `grep -o '"holder":[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"'`; the `[^"]*` class stops at the first `"` character, so a holder whose JSON-escaped form contains `\"` (an escaped double-quote, written by `claim_coordinator_claim`'s `sed 's/"/\\"/g'`) is silently truncated — the regex matches only the bytes before the escaped quote.
findings.trigger: A holder string containing a literal double-quote character (e.g. a machine name or run-id containing `"`); `claim_coordinator_claim` JSON-escapes it to `\"`, but `[^"]*` stops at the unescaped `"` byte, returning a truncated `raw_holder` to the outer `sed` extraction, which then strips only up to the first `"` it sees.
findings.accepted_if: The holder string as printed in the run's refusal output is identical to the holder string embedded in the run-status comment's `<!-- zbuild-holder: -->` field, even when that string contains a double-quote character.

findings.message: The DSCLA-4 unit-test block pre-seeds the run-status comment file with a hand-written `<!-- zbuild-holder: ... -->` line instead of calling `rsc_render_header` to generate it; if `rsc_render_header` changes its holder-comment format and `_ccgl_read_holder`'s regex is not updated to match, this test still passes (the hand-written fixture still matches the stale reader) while the production round-trip is broken.
findings.quote:
cat > "$ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE/$_dscla4_issue/run-status-comment.txt" <<'RSCEOF'
<!-- zbuild-run-status run_id=holder-run-99 -->
<!-- zbuild-holder: run-holder-99 on machine-other -->
run is in progress...
RSCEOF
findings.trigger: A change to `rsc_render_header`'s `<!-- zbuild-holder: %>` output format that is not matched by a corresponding update to `_ccgl_read_holder`'s regex; the DSCLA-4 unit test passes because it reads the hand-written old-format fixture, while the DSCLA-9/15 integration tests (which use `rsc_render_header`) would fail.
findings.accepted_if: The DSCLA-4 unit test generates its run-status comment fixture using `rsc_render_header` (the same code that writes it in production), so a format divergence between the writer and the reader is caught at the unit level, not only in integration.
